top_signals.title: ASEAN Moves to Build Emergency Oil Reserves Amid Iran Supply Crisis
top_signals.summary: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations has agreed to set up a joint crude oil stockpiling scheme in response to the supply disruption from the war in Iran, which severely affected countries in the region. The scheme will comprise storage sites in Indonesia and Thailand, Reuters reported today, from which ASEAN members will draw oil in times of tight supply. The withdrawals will be based on a ticket system, under which member countries would pay an advance fee to reserve the right to purchase a certain volume of oil or fuel from storage sites…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Druley: Avoid Crowded Trades When It Comes to Investment
top_signals.summary: In a November 12, 2026 interview on Bloomberg’s Horizon’s Middle East and Africa, Cambridge Associates CEO David Druley discussed how a shift from efficiency to self-sufficiency is reshaping global investment strategies. He warned that equity markets are highly concentrated, with roughly 10 stocks comprising 35–40% of U.S. indices and large portions of global and emerging markets, making diversification more critical than ever. Druley expects only a temporary pause in U.S. AI and data center expansion, viewing it as an opportunity for the UAE and Saudi Arabia. He highlighted geopolitical constraints on U.S. investment in Chinese venture capital as a chance for Middle Eastern and European investors, and emphasized the growing sophistication of regional asset managers and the pivotal role of large family offices, which account for 40% of his firm’s business. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.
